books.section: A. The Ascendancy of the New Right

stem: Which of the following did NOT contribute to the federal deficits of the Reagan years?

options.misconception: The passage says tax cuts left the government collecting less than it spent.
The passage says Reagan raised military spending sharply alongside the tax cuts.

options.text: Tax breaks that favored wealthy individuals
options.misconception: Background: cutting taxes on the wealthy was part of the supply-side program, and it drained revenue.

options.text: A surge in federal education spending

rationales.A: The passage says tax cuts left the government collecting less than it spent.
rationales.B: The passage says Reagan raised military spending sharply alongside the tax cuts.
rationales.C: Background: cutting taxes on wealthy individuals was part of the supply-side program, and it drained revenue.
rationales.D: Background: education spending stagnated in the 1980s; the deficits came from tax cuts and the military buildup.
rationales.general:
1. Work the recipe for a deficit: spend more than you collect.
2. The passage gives both halves: tax cuts shrank what came in, and the buildup raised what went out.
3. Background: the debt more than doubled between 1980 and 1986.
4. Education spending is the odd one out — it stagnated, so it cannot explain the gap.
Remember: a deficit has two handles, revenue and spending — check both.

stimulus.source_note: Original summary based on Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 11, and Princeton Review, Chapter 13.
stimulus.text: Original summary based on the grounding books: President Ronald Reagan's economic program, called Reaganomics, rested on supply-side theory: cutting taxes on businesses and wealthy individuals, the argument ran, would spur investment, and the growth that followed would benefit everyone. At the same time, Reagan raised military spending sharply. Tax cuts plus the buildup meant the government spent far more than it collected, and the national debt more than doubled between 1980 and 1986.
